response.basis: Reviewed all 13 numbered NL segments against the primary plan's 37 contracts and 7 transition groups; cross-checked containment completeness pass requirement (item 1) which requires separate containment contracts for every explicit child/substate relation and for the complete source-and-alternative group under a continuing owner, finding several named substates without containment rows.
response.reason: The primary plan captures all endpoint, initial-entry, termination, and top-level containment-of-target contracts, but under the containment-discipline rule (preserve containment for every named substate under a continuing owner, including sources sharing a group with already-contained siblings), it omits containment rows for: InitialState itself as sibling under AutonomousMode; cruise and lane_change under HighwayMode; lane_change_urban, straight, and intersection under UrbanMode (only enter_urban was covered); exit_urban under UrbanMode; and collision_avoidance_active under the collision-avoidance scope. No new transition groups are needed since all transition relations in the NL are already represented in the primary plan's transition_groups (NL6, NL10, NL11, NL12, NL13 relations are single-alternative and correctly emitted as standalone endpoint contracts rather than groups).

additional_contracts.basis: NL12 explicit compound guard with mode-dependent sub-thresholds establishes a distinguishability concern independent of the endpoint existence obligation.
additional_contracts.normative_statement: The activation guard for collision_avoidance_active is a compound disjunctive condition covering pedestrian detection, rear-distance/velocity, and mode-dependent front-distance sub-conditions; each disjunct must remain distinguishable within the compound guard.
additional_contracts.quote: detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode
additional_contracts.reason: NL12 lists three independently evaluated disjuncts (pedestrian_detected; dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30; mode-dependent front distance) composing one guard; the primary plan preserves this as a single compound guard string in NL12-ENDPOINT-1 but does not separately preserve the mutual-exclusivity/distinguishability obligation implied by mode-dependent thresholds (15m highway vs 10m urban) which depend on the concurrently active driving mode.

result.basis: Reviewed all 13 numbered NL segments against the primary plan's 37 contracts and 7 transition groups; cross-checked containment completeness pass requirement (item 1) which requires separate containment contracts for every explicit child/substate relation and for the complete source-and-alternative group under a continuing owner, finding several named substates without containment rows.
result.reason: The primary plan captures all endpoint, initial-entry, termination, and top-level containment-of-target contracts, but under the containment-discipline rule (preserve containment for every named substate under a continuing owner, including sources sharing a group with already-contained siblings), it omits containment rows for: InitialState itself as sibling under AutonomousMode; cruise and lane_change under HighwayMode; lane_change_urban, straight, and intersection under UrbanMode (only enter_urban was covered); exit_urban under UrbanMode; and collision_avoidance_active under the collision-avoidance scope. These are independently violable containment obligations distinct from the endpoint/initial-entry contracts already present. One additional guard_disjointness obligation over the NL12 compound activation guard's mode-dependent sub-thresholds is also added since the primary plan preserves it only as a single guard string without a distinguishability contract, unlike the parallel treatment given to NL2/NL3/NL7 guard groups. No new transition groups are needed since all transition relations in the NL are already represented in the primary plan's transition_groups (NL6, NL10, NL11, NL12, NL13 relations are single-alternative and correctly emitted as standalone endpoint contracts rather than groups).

Both are flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, both are reachable_from_initial=false in inspection_equivalent_facts, and both are verify-refuted (kind=initial_entry, status=refuted) because an initial pseudostate edge should be unconditional. (4) No LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/deadlock-frontier diagnostic was present in the supplied facts, so no V1 deadlock candidate is emitted absent that certificate. (5) Event-consumer coverage for NL11-EVENTCOV-1 shows declared and reachable consumer sets matching (no narrower reachable set found), so no separate coverage defect is raised there beyond the endpoint/reachability issues above.

(2) The AutonomousMode-level HighwayMode<->UrbanMode dynamic switch (NL11) is implemented as a two-step token-routing mechanism whose completing edges are nested initial pseudostate transitions (transition:line:82 target HighwayMode guard R45RouteToken==22, and transition:line:85 target UrbanMode guard R45RouteToken==23). Both are flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, both are reachable_from_initial=false in inspection_equivalent_facts, and both are verify-refuted (kind=initial_entry, status=refuted) because an initial pseudostate edge should be unconditional. Because these completing edges are unreachable from the machine's actual initial configuration, the NL11 cross-mode-switch behavior is not operationally realized as a whole, even though separate endpoint transitions exist elsewhere. This is a distinct reachability/operational-completion property from the plain endpoint-existence contracts. (3) FinishState (the designated termination target for both NL6 and NL10) has two reachable outgoing edges (transition:line:90 triggered by high_way_true, transition:line:92 triggered by urban_way_true) that reset the route token and re-enter the HighwayMode/UrbanMode machinery, so FinishState is not a stable completion sink -- this undermines the stable-termination property of NL6-TERM-1 and NL10-TERM-1 independent of the fact that the FinishState-reaching endpoint transitions themselves exist. (4) No LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/deadlock-frontier diagnostic was present in the supplied facts, so no V1 deadlock candidate is emitted absent that certificate. (5) Event-consumer coverage for NL11-EVENTCOV-1 shows declared and reachable consumer sets matching (no narrower reachable set found), so no separate coverage defect is raised there beyond the endpoint/reachability issues above.

result.reason: Behavioral-consequence audit examined root reachability, event-consumer coverage, forbidden/malformed initial edges, dead-end frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination against the closed FCSTM and its deterministic inspection/verify facts. Key findings: (1) HighwayMode and UrbanMode both terminate through a shared route-token variable (R45RouteToken); HighwayMode->FinishState (guard R45RouteToken==12) and UrbanMode->FinishState (guard R45RouteToken==21) exist and are reachable. (2) The AutonomousMode-level HighwayMode<->UrbanMode dynamic switch (NL11) is implemented as a two-step token-routing mechanism whose completing edges are nested initial pseudostate transitions (transition:line:82 target HighwayMode guard R45RouteToken==22, and transition:line:85 target UrbanMode guard R45RouteToken==23). Both are flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, both are reachable_from_initial=false in inspection_equivalent_facts, and both are verify-refuted (kind=initial_entry, status=refuted) because an initial pseudostate edge should be unconditional. Because these completing edges are unreachable from the machine's actual initial configuration, the NL11 cross-mode-switch behavior is not operationally realized as a whole, even though separate endpoint transitions exist elsewhere. This is a distinct reachability/operational-completion property from the plain endpoint-existence contracts. (3) FinishState (the designated termination target for both NL6 and NL10) has two reachable outgoing edges (transition:line:90 triggered by high_way_true, transition:line:92 triggered by urban_way_true) that reset the route token and re-enter the HighwayMode/UrbanMode machinery, so FinishState is not a stable completion sink -- this undermines the stable-termination property of NL6-TERM-1 and NL10-TERM-1 independent of the fact that the FinishState-reaching endpoint transitions themselves exist. (4) No LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/deadlock-frontier diagnostic was present in the supplied facts, so no V1 deadlock candidate is emitted absent that certificate. (5) Event-consumer coverage for NL11-EVENTCOV-1 shows declared and reachable consumer sets matching (no narrower reachable set found), so no separate coverage defect is raised there beyond the endpoint/reachability issues above.

response.basis: Reviewed all 13 numbered NL segments against the primary plan's 37 contracts and 7 transition groups; cross-checked containment completeness pass requirement (item 1) which requires separate containment contracts for every explicit child/substate relation and for the complete source-and-alternative group under a continuing owner, finding several named substates without containment rows.
response.reason: The primary plan captures all endpoint, initial-entry, termination, and top-level containment-of-target contracts, but under the containment-discipline rule (preserve containment for every named substate under a continuing owner, including sources sharing a group with already-contained siblings), it omits containment rows for: InitialState itself as sibling under AutonomousMode; cruise and lane_change under HighwayMode; lane_change_urban, straight, and intersection under UrbanMode (only enter_urban was covered); exit_urban under UrbanMode; and collision_avoidance_active under the collision-avoidance scope. These are independently violable containment obligations distinct from the endpoint/initial-entry contracts already present. One additional guard_disjointness obligation over the NL12 compound activation guard's mode-dependent sub-thresholds is also added since the primary plan preserves it only as a single guard string without a distinguishability contract, unlike the parallel treatment given to NL2/NL3/NL7 guard groups. No new transition groups are needed since all transition relations in the NL are already represented in the primary plan's transition_groups (NL6, NL10, NL11, NL12, NL13 relations are single-alternative and correctly emitted as standalone endpoint contracts rather than groups).

branches.reason: Behavioral-consequence audit examined root reachability, event-consumer coverage, forbidden/malformed initial edges, dead-end frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination against the closed FCSTM and its deterministic inspection/verify facts. Key findings: (1) HighwayMode and UrbanMode both terminate through a shared route-token variable (R45RouteToken); HighwayMode->FinishState (guard R45RouteToken==12) and UrbanMode->FinishState (guard R45RouteToken==21) exist and are reachable. (2) The AutonomousMode-level HighwayMode<->UrbanMode dynamic switch (NL11) is implemented as a two-step token-routing mechanism whose completing edges are nested initial pseudostate transitions (transition:line:82 target HighwayMode guard R45RouteToken==22, and transition:line:85 target UrbanMode guard R45RouteToken==23). Both are flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, both are reachable_from_initial=false in inspection_equivalent_facts, and both are verify-refuted (kind=initial_entry, status=refuted) because an initial pseudostate edge should be unconditional. Because these completing edges are unreachable from the machine's actual initial configuration, the NL11 cross-mode-switch behavior is not operationally realized as a whole, even though separate endpoint transitions exist elsewhere. This is a distinct reachability/operational-completion property from the plain endpoint-existence contracts. (3) FinishState (the designated termination target for both NL6 and NL10) has two reachable outgoing edges (transition:line:90 triggered by high_way_true, transition:line:92 triggered by urban_way_true) that reset the route token and re-enter the HighwayMode/UrbanMode machinery, so FinishState is not a stable completion sink -- this undermines the stable-termination property of NL6-TERM-1 and NL10-TERM-1 independent of the fact that the FinishState-reaching endpoint transitions themselves exist. (4) No LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/deadlock-frontier diagnostic was present in the supplied facts, so no V1 deadlock candidate is emitted absent that certificate. (5) Event-consumer coverage for NL11-EVENTCOV-1 shows declared and reachable consumer sets matching (no narrower reachable set found), so no separate coverage defect is raised there beyond the endpoint/reachability issues above.
